manifestations.description: Right leg and ankle pains which would grow worse after prolonged sitting or walking.
He could tolerate walking for one hour.
Needed holding onto rails for going downstairs.
Less confident in climbing and walking on uneven grounds in construction sites.
Multiple scars on the right leg.
Walking with a slight limping gait.
Less steady weight bearing capacity on the right leg.
Marked muscle wasting of the right lower limb.
Ankle motion was restricted in all pains, virtually nil with inversion or eversion.

He can no longer jump or run; he cannot squat fully; difficulties when going up and down stairs; cannot climb up and jump down from heights without assistance and without ladders and other structures to help him climb up and down for inspecting works.

treatments_received: sent to the Accident and Emergency Department of Queen Mary Hospital
suture of skin and subcutaneous tissue of other sites (right leg wound)
open reduction of dislocation of ankle
application of external fixation of compound fracture at tibia and fibula
further debridement of the right leg wound
transferred to Maclehose Medical Rehabitation Centre for non-weight bearing walking exercise
removal of the syndesmosis screw and external fixator
examination under anaesthetic of the right distal tibiofibular syndesmosis and syndesmosis screw insertion
physiotherapy (26 sessions at Alice Ho Mui Ling Nethersole Hospital)
rehabilitation and mobilization exercises at MMRC

losses.description: Experienced difficulties when going up and down stairs; less steady weight bearing; restricted ankle motion; cannot jump or run; cannot squat fully; less confident in climbing and walking on uneven grounds.
Multiple scars on the right leg.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Can no longer jump or run.
Cannot climb up and jump down from heights without assistance and without ladders and other structures to help him climb up and down for inspecting works.

Plaintiff would have been promoted in October 2000 if he had not been injured; the Plaintiff's disabilities would have impact on the Plaintiff's future prospects and there is a real and substantial risk that the Plaintiff might lose his current job and be at a disadvantage in the open labour market.

comparable_cases.injury_description: the plaintiff suffered 15% impairment of the whole person and was granted one year sick leave. His injuries seemed very similar to those of the Plaintiff in this case.
